h: Cheese, caves and the little city next door
p: Here's a fun fact for cheese lovers: the constant cool temperature underground makes the caves perfect for maturing cheddar, and cave-aged cheese has been matured at Wookey Hole for years. Keep an eye out for it in the shop, as it makes a great edible souvenir and a nice talking point at home.

The River Axe is the real sculptor here. It has carved its way through the Mendip limestone over thousands of years, and you'll see its clear, green-blue water running through the chambers. It emerges outside the caves and once powered the paper mill, so it ties the whole site together.

How long should you allow? With the cave tour, the mill and the family attractions, most people spend a good part of the day here. If you've got younger children who want to do everything, plan for a full day with a proper lunch break in the middle.

Tips for your visit: book ahead for busy weekends and holidays, wear comfy shoes for walking between areas, and bring a layer for the caves. If anyone in your group can't manage the cave, there's still lots to enjoy above ground.

Wells is only a couple of miles away and makes a perfect add-on. It's England's smallest city, with a magnificent cathedral, the moated Bishop's Palace and Vicar's Close, often described as one of the oldest continuously inhabited residential streets in Europe. Glastonbury, with its famous Tor, is also within easy reach, so you could easily turn this into a weekend of exploring this corner of Somerset.
